title: Smooth finite-type atlases and proper diagonals for Deligne--Mumford moduli stacks
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-scheme], and let $\mathcal F$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack on $\mathit{Sch}/S$ in the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. A smooth finite-type atlas means an $S$-scheme $U$ and a representable surjective etale morphism $h_U\to\mathcal F$ such that $U\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. On DM stacks over a field, existence of such an atlas expresses smoothness and finite type, including quasi-compactness. For a scheme $S$ and a DM stack $\mathcal F$ over $S$, a proper diagonal means the following scheme-test condition: for every pair of $S$-schemes $T,U$ and maps $a:h_T\to\mathcal F$, $b:h_U\to\mathcal F$, the 2-fibre product $h_T\times_{\mathcal F}h_U$ is equivalent over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ to $h_R$ for an $S$-scheme $R$, compatibly with both projections $p:R\to T$ and $q:R\to U$, and the induced morphism $R\to T\times_S U$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Compatibility means natural isomorphisms over identity base maps, not merely equivalences of abstract categories. On DM stacks this is exactly separatedness: a proper unramified diagonal is finite and therefore representable by schemes. These predicates do not assert that any particular moduli stack has an atlas or a proper diagonal.
